intro: Read, Write, Edit, Bash, Grep, Glob: what Claude Code is actually doing when those lines scroll by.

1.summary: What a tool call is, and the six core tools.

lesson.title: What's a tool call?
lesson.body:
A model can only produce text. So how does Claude Code edit files?

It writes a structured request, a **tool call**, that says "please run the Read tool on `src/app.js`." The **harness** (Claude Code) actually performs the action, then hands the result back to the model as new text in its context. The model reads the result and decides what to do next.

Think of a surgeon saying "scalpel": the surgeon decides, and the nurse hands it over. Every line like `Read(src/app.js)` or `Bash(npm test)` you see scrolling by is one of those requests.
lesson.pm: This request, act, result, decide loop is the core of every AI agent, not just coding ones. Once you see it here, you'll recognize it everywhere.

lesson.title: The six core tools
lesson.body:
- **Read** opens a file and reads it. Changes nothing.
- **Write** creates a new file, or replaces an entire file.
- **Edit** changes specific text inside an existing file, like find-and-replace. It's safer and more precise than rewriting the whole file.
- **Bash** runs a terminal command (tests, git, installs...).
- **Grep** searches *inside* files for text, e.g. every place "checkout" appears.
- **Glob** finds files by *name pattern*, e.g. `**/*.json` = every JSON file in every folder.

Read, Grep and Glob only look around. Write, Edit and Bash can change things, which is why those are the ones that ask your permission.
lesson.pm: A long run of Read/Grep/Glob calls means Claude is still exploring. The Edits are where the real change happens, so that's where your review attention should go.

cards.back: A structured request from the model asking the harness to perform an action (read a file, run a command). The result comes back into context.
Opens and reads a file. Doesn't change anything.
Write creates or fully replaces a file. Edit changes specific text inside an existing file.
Runs a terminal (shell) command, e.g. `npm test` or `git status`.
Searches inside files for matching text.
Finds files by name pattern, e.g. `**/*.json` = all JSON files in all folders.

quiz.q: Claude needs every file that mentions "paywall". Which tool fits?
quiz.why: Grep searches inside files. Glob only matches file names.

quiz.q: What does this tool call do?
options: Finds files whose names end in .test.js
Runs every test file in the project
Creates a new test file in each folder
quiz.why: Glob matches file names by pattern. `**` means any folder depth.

quiz.q: What's the difference between Write and Edit?
options: Write replaces a whole file; Edit changes part
Write changes part; Edit replaces a whole file
Write is for code; Edit is for text files
Write saves locally; Edit saves to Bitbucket
quiz.why: Write creates or fully replaces a file. Edit swaps specific text inside one.

quiz.q: Which of these tools only looks and never changes anything?
quiz.why: Glob just finds files by name. Bash, Write and Edit can all change things.

options: The model asking the harness to take an action
The harness asking the model for a reply
A network call between Claude and a server
A command you type into the terminal yourself
quiz.why: The model writes a structured request; the harness performs it and returns the result.

2.summary: Web tools, subagents, MCP tools, diffs and parallel calls.

lesson.title: More tools: web, subagents and MCP
lesson.body:
- **WebSearch** searches the internet. **WebFetch** reads one specific web page.
- **Agent** (a **subagent**) spins up a helper Claude with its own fresh context window for a side task, like "find everywhere we call the payments API." It works independently and reports back a short summary. Think of delegating to an intern who returns a memo instead of their whole notebook. This keeps the main conversation's context clean.
- **Todo / task lists**: Claude writes a checklist for multi-step work and ticks items off, so you can see progress.
- **MCP tools** come from services you connect, like Jira, Slack or a database. **MCP** (Model Context Protocol) is a standard plug shape that lets any tool connect to any AI harness. Their names look like `mcp__jira__search`.
lesson.pm: MCP is why "can our AI talk to X?" is increasingly a configuration question rather than an engineering project. Worth knowing when scoping AI features.

lesson.title: Reading tool calls like a pro
lesson.body:
A tool call has a **name** and an **input**:

```
Bash(git status)
Edit(src/Header.tsx)
```

For Edit, Claude Code shows a **diff**, the before and after: lines starting with `-` (red) are removed, lines with `+` (green) are added. Reading diffs is the single most useful review skill.

You'll often see several calls fire at once. Those are **parallel tool calls**: independent actions (like reading three files) done simultaneously to save time.

If you **deny** a permission prompt, Claude doesn't crash. It gets told "the user said no" and tries another approach or asks you.
lesson.pm: You don't need to understand every line of a diff. Check that the *size* and *location* of the change match what you asked for. Surprises there are worth a question.

cards.back: A helper Claude with its own fresh context that handles a side task and reports back a summary.
WebSearch searches the internet. WebFetch reads one specific page.
Model Context Protocol: a standard way to plug outside tools and data (Jira, Slack, databases) into AI apps.
A before/after view of a change. `-` lines were removed and `+` lines were added.
Several independent tool calls run at the same time to save time.

quiz.q: Why does Claude Code hand a big search to a subagent?
options: It keeps the main context window clean
Subagents always run on a cheaper model
Subagents are allowed to skip permissions
Subagents can read files Claude can't open
quiz.why: The subagent works in its own context and reports back only a summary.

quiz.q: In a diff, what does a line starting with `+` mean?
Where does a tool named `mcp__jira__create_issue` come from?
quiz.why: Tools prefixed `mcp__` come from MCP servers, connectors to outside services.

options: A standard for plugging tools into AI apps
A model that specializes in writing code
A file format for Claude Code settings
A method for compressing long prompts
quiz.why: Model Context Protocol: one plug shape so any tool can connect to any AI harness.

quiz.q: Claude has a link to one docs page it needs. Which tool reads it?
quiz.why: WebFetch reads a specific URL. WebSearch finds pages; Read and Grep work on local files.
